title: A 1.11pJ/b 224Gb/s XSR Receiver with Slice-Based CTLE and PI-Based Clock Generator in 12nm CMOS
problem: Extra-short reach (XSR) 224Gb/s receivers at 112Gb/s-equivalent require both CTLE bandwidth doubling and 8x sampling frequency increase while maintaining strict power and area constraints.
motivation: As transceiver data rates scale to 224Gb/s for short-reach links, analog receiver architectures must double CTLE bandwidth and increase sampling frequency simultaneously without exceeding power and area budgets.
method: Extra-short reach receiver using slice-based continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) and phase-interpolator (PI)-based eight-phase clock generator, enabling efficient bandwidth scaling in 12nm CMOS. Slicing CTLE distributes filtering across multiple stages.
key_novelty: Slice-based CTLE architecture enabling efficient bandwidth scaling to 224Gb/s while maintaining power efficiency (1.11pJ/bit).
contributions: Slice-based CTLE enabling bandwidth doubling with distributed equalization
PI-based eight-phase clock generator for precise multi-phase timing
primary_theme: 224Gb/s extra-short reach receiver with slice-based equalization
